supportProfile.description: The deployment profile the values claim. P1, the default, is the profile the threat model covers: the render fails, listing each departure, when a value leaves it (DinD, executor.workerAuth.mode legacy, a credential proxy off or a credentialIsolation override, a harness not qualified with both proxies, harnessContainer shared, a worker securityContext below restricted, the sandbox executor, claudeRunner, or networkPolicy.enabled false). unsupported renders such values and lists the departures in the install notes; the threat model does not cover that deployment (ADR-0154, finding F-11).

workerAdmission.description: Native ValidatingAdmissionPolicy over every ploeg-worker Pod in the release namespace (Kubernetes 1.30 or later); see docs/ops/self-hosting-security.md.

enabled.description: Install the policy and its Deny binding. The render fails on Kubernetes older than 1.30 and on any team or Role that keeps privileged DinD. Installing it needs cluster-scoped RBAC for admissionregistration.k8s.io.

runtimeClassNames.description: RuntimeClass names a worker Pod must select. Empty leaves the runtime class unchecked; a non-empty list refuses a worker Pod without one of them. The chart does not install the handler.

fullnameOverride.description: Object name prefix; empty = the Helm release name

instanceOverride.description: app.kubernetes.io/instance label; empty = the Helm release name

networkPolicy.description: Default-deny NetworkPolicies for every pod the chart renders (ploegd, workers, the sandbox launcher, claude-runner, ploeg-mcp), each with the allowlist that pod needs. Egress to an endpoint is derived from its URL unless `peers` names it: an IP is itself, a bare name is the release namespace, `name.ns.svc` is that namespace, anything else is the internet outside `privateCidrs`, on the URL's port or the scheme's default. The policies are plain `networking.k8s.io/v1` objects and are applied only by a CNI that enforces NetworkPolicy (Cilium, Calico, Antrea); kind's kindnet and Flannel ignore them. An installer's own policies add to these, never subtract (docs/ops/network.md).

enabled.description: Render the policies. `false` renders none and leaves the network to the installer, which the threat model records as finding F-02.

dns.description: The cluster DNS every policy allows. The default selects CoreDNS as kubeadm, kind and Talos label it; a cluster with another label names its own peers.

privateCidrs.description: CIDRs an internet rule excludes, so a pod allowed to reach a public host cannot reach the cluster, the nodes or the LAN through the same rule. Add your pod, service and node ranges when they are outside RFC 1918.

database.description: ploegd's PostgreSQL. The connection URI lives in a Secret the chart cannot read, so there is nothing to derive: empty `peers` allows every pod in the release namespace on `port`.

port.description: The PostgreSQL port as the pod listens on it.

gateway.description: The model gateway: ploegd reaches `executor.litellm.adminUrl` and workers `executor.litellm.baseUrl`. Empty `peers` derives the destination from each URL.

forge.description: The forges: workers reach the executor's forge `url`; ploegd and claude-runner reach every configured forge's `publicUrl` or `url`, and api.github.com for github.com. Empty `peers` derives the destination from each URL.

tracker.description: The trackers ploegd calls: `tracker.url`, ClickUp when a ClickUp Secret is set, the GitHub API when `tracker.github.appId` is set. Empty `peers` derives the destination from each URL.

knowledgeGraph.description: The Omnigraph server at `knowledgeGraph.url`, reached by ploegd only. Empty `peers` derives the destination from the URL.

telemetry.description: Every OTLP collector a harness `telemetry.endpoint` or `claudeRunner.env.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` names. Empty `peers` derives the destination from each URL.

kubernetesApi.description: The Kubernetes API the sandbox launcher creates SandboxClaims through. The API server is not a pod, so empty `peers` allows any peer on `ports`; name its endpoint addresses as ipBlocks to narrow it, or add your CNI's API-server entity in a policy of your own.

ingressFrom.description: Peers that may reach ploegd on 8080: the gateway that forwards webhooks, operator consumers, Prometheus. Empty allows any peer on that port, because the chart cannot know your gateway; set, the policy allows these peers plus this release's own worker, launcher, ploeg-mcp and claude-runner pods.

extraEgress.description: Further egress rules for ploegd, such as a tracker or forge whose URL the derivation cannot place.
Further egress rules for every worker pod, such as the registry a DinD sidecar pulls from or the allowlist proxy of ADR-0037. Each rule widens what a model-directed harness can reach.

ingressFrom.description: Peers that may reach ploeg-mcp on `mcp.port`. Empty allows any peer on that port; `mcp.networkPolicy.ingress` is the older per-component form and still renders.

pool.description: ploegd's connection pool as the PLOEG_DB_* variables; a setting the connection URI names wins; null leaves ploegd's default

digest.description: Digest of the appVersion image; the release writes it into the published chart

image.description: The ploeg-worker image (ADR-0138): ploeg-worker, git and CA certificates from Wolfi on an empty base, with no shell (ADR-0144). It runs the worker container when the harness runs in its own container and provides the launcher binary the harness container runs; executor.workerImage overrides it.

digest.description: Digest of the appVersion image; the release writes it into the published chart
Digest of the appVersion image; the release writes it into the published chart

install.description: Install Claude Code from Anthropic's signed release into the runner pod before it starts; false when the image already carries it

version.description: Claude Code version to install; empty uses the image's pin

sha256.description: Expected sha256 of the version's Linux binary; empty trusts the signed manifest alone

selector.description: PromQL label matchers applied to every alert; empty = job and namespace of this release

runbookBaseUrl.description: URL of the rendered alerts page; each alert appends its anchor

reviewTokenSecret.description: ADR-0122: the Secret holding the Tenant's review actor token, which writes accepted Client and Tenant promotions to conceptsGraph. Unset leaves them waiting.

transactionToken.description: ADR-0156: the key ploegd signs each Run's transaction token with (PLOEG_TRANSACTION_TOKEN_*). Empty signs none. With a key, every executor.teams[] Team needs config.teams.<name>.sponsor.

issuer.description: The URL ploegd is reached at, the token's iss (PLOEG_TRANSACTION_TOKEN_ISSUER). Required with signingKeySecret.

audience.description: Ploeg's trust domain, the token's aud: an http(s) URL or a urn: (PLOEG_TRANSACTION_TOKEN_AUDIENCE). Empty is the issuer.

signingKeySecret.description: Secret name and key of the PEM P-256 private key ploegd signs transaction tokens with (PLOEG_TRANSACTION_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY). Unset signs none.

retiredKeysSecret.description: Secret name and key of the PEM public keys ploegd still publishes after a rotation (PLOEG_TRANSACTION_TOKEN_RETIRED_KEYS). Keep a retired key one lease TTL.

runIdentity.description: ADR-0149: the key ploegd signs Run identities with (PLOEG_RUN_IDENTITY_*). Empty issues none.

teams.description: Teams whose Work Items the consumer may read and act on. ["*"] grants every Team; an empty list grants none. Required, so no consumer reads every Team by leaving it out.

readContent.description: Grants reading what agents and people wrote beyond Work Item metadata: Run transcripts and briefings, the context people attached and Work Item Note reviews. Unset follows execute: an executing consumer reads them, a read-only one does not.

clientIds.description: Client ids whose person tokens (ADR-0150) make this consumer the caller when the token's azp names them and its aud is operator.personTokens.audience; needs operator.personTokens.

audiences.description: Audiences of person tokens (ADR-0150) issued for this consumer alone; a token whose aud names one makes this consumer the caller, and its azp may equal that audience. No other consumer may list it or name it as a client id. Needs operator.personTokens.

personTokens.description: ADR-0150: verify person tokens, JWTs an identity provider issued on a person's behalf for a consumer's audiences or for Ploeg's shared audience. Forwarded as PLOEG_OPERATOR_PERSON_*; issuer is required once any field is set, and audience once a consumer names clientIds.

harnessContainer.description: separate (the default) runs the harness in its own container of the Run's pod, behind ploeg-worker harness-serve, with no credential in its environment, while the worker container keeps every credential and both proxies (ADR-0138). A workload with DinD, a credential proxy off or harness claude-environment keeps shared. shared runs the harness in the worker's container; deprecated, removed in the minor after 0.2.

workerContainerResources.description: Resources of the worker container when the harness runs in its own container; the harness container keeps workerResources.

workerContainerSecurityContext.description: Merged over the worker container's default context when the harness runs in its own container: restricted, a read-only root filesystem, and the uid and gid of workerSecurityContext (1000 when it names none), because both containers write the shared work directory.

defaultTarget.description: fallback repo for teams that declare none; empty = a team with no repoOwner/repoName gets no env target and relies entirely on the work item's resolved target

perRunBudget.//: Per-run key ceiling for a team with no plan. Optional; falls back to budget, which for a PLANNED team is the Shift pool and not a per-run figure.

litellmTeamId.//: ADR-0078: the LiteLLM team_id every Run key of this team is minted in. Optional; empty = no team.

mcpAccessGroups.//: ADR-0078: read-only LiteLLM MCP access groups granted to this team's Run keys; needs litellmTeamId. Optional; empty = no MCP tools.

maxRunning.description: Concurrency cap: the most Runs this team may have running at once, enforced by ploegd at claim time. A claim over the cap gets no work and the worker exits 0. Every workload's maxReplicaCount is clamped to it. 0 or unset = unlimited.

spendCap.description: This team's spend cap per calendar period (ADR-0162), in place of executor.spendCap; config.teams.<name>.spendCap wins over both. usd 0 = no cap, which leaves profile P1.

runtimeClassName.description: This team's worker RuntimeClass under every executor type; a Role's runtimeClassName overrides it. Empty = executor.runtimeClassName.

plan.description: ordered Rounds of a Shift (run-multi-agent-shifts): each round a reader fan-out or one writer. A team with a plan runs multi-role; without one, dispatch is unchanged. budget doubles as the Shift pool.

maxFixRounds.description: ADR-0017: how many times a reviewer request_changes may re-open the writing Round of this plan. 0 = loop off, the plan runs to exhaustion.

executorType.description: Optional: this team's executor while executor.type is keda or sandbox; unset = executor.type. Lets one team run under the experimental sandbox executor while the others stay on keda.

harnesses.description: ADR-0098/ADR-0099, planned teams only: the Harnesses an operator admission may choose per Run. Each entry renders its own workload per Role and replaces the Role's harness block; unset = the one configured harness.

allowUnqualifiedHarnesses.description: ADR-0098: admit an allowed Harness that is not qualified even when it is not the Role's default. Default false.

items.//: repoOwner/repoName are NOT required: the repository belongs to the work item, resolved at ingest (R11). They remain as a per-team fallback while teams migrate.

forge.description: Which forge the workers act against; selects the sibling block of the same name. Also the default dialect for a Work Item whose target names no forge (ADR-0023). One active forge per release: a worker pod holds one forge URL and one credential.

url.description: Web root, https://github.com or a GitHub Enterprise Server root; the REST API is derived. Empty = ploegd configures no GitHub forge provider.

tokenSecret.description: The workers' boot credential (AGENT_BUILDER_TOKEN) and, without a GitHub App, the shared credential writing Runs push with. With tracker.github.appId set, writing Runs get a per-Run installation token instead (ADR-0086).

readTokenSecret.description: ADR-0013 tier 1: a read-only fine-grained token for reading Roles. Required (name and key) when any team has a reading Role.

webhookSecret.description: Verifies X-Hub-Signature-256 on POST /webhooks/forge/github. Unset = every GitHub forge webhook is rejected.

botLogin.description: The GitHub App's bot login, e.g. ploeg[bot], so Ploeg's own reviews never trigger rework.

url.description: Base URL, no /api/v4. Empty = ploegd configures no GitLab provider, so findings never reach a merge request.

publicUrl.description: ploegd's GitLab URL when it differs from the workers' url. Empty = url.

tokenSecret.description: Token with api scope on the target projects, sent as PRIVATE-TOKEN. ADR-0013 tier 2 does not apply on GitLab: per-run push credentials are minted through a Forgejo admin endpoint with no GitLab equivalent, so this shared token is what writing Runs use.

readTokenSecret.description: ADR-0013 tier 1, as for forgejo: a read-only credential for reading Roles, so the reader/writer split is enforced at the forge and not only by scheduling. On GitLab a second project access token at read_repository scope. Required (name and key) when any team has a reading Role: the render fails without it rather than hand readers the read-write token.

webhookSecret.description: Shared secret GitLab sends as X-Gitlab-Token to POST /webhooks/forge/gitlab. Unset = every forge webhook is rejected.

url.description: The workers' forge URL (FORGE_URL): clone, push, pull-request API and the forge proxy upstream. An in-cluster URL keeps Run traffic off the public gateway. Required when the executor is enabled on this forge; empty with the executor off = ploegd has no forge provider.

publicUrl.description: ploegd's forge URL (PLOEG_FORGEJO_URL). Empty = url. Set it to the public https URL when url is in-cluster: ploegd matches a consumer's https repository URLs against it and accepts only https or ssh ones.

readTokenSecret.description: ADR-0013 tier 1: read-only credential for reading Roles. Required (name and key) when any team has a reading Role: the render fails without it rather than hand readers the read-write builder token.

botPasswordSecret.description: ADR-0013 tier 2: the password of botUser, which ploegd uses to MINT per-run push tokens limited to the Run's repository. Held only by ploegd, never by a worker. Unset = nothing is minted.

botUser.description: the forge user whose tokens are minted (default agent-builder)

webhookSecret.description: HMAC secret that verifies X-Forgejo-Signature on POST /webhooks/forge/forgejo. Unset = every forge webhook is rejected: merges are still found by the periodic pull request reconcile, but human reviews and failed checks never reach Ploeg.

serviceAccount.description: Worker pods ServiceAccount. create and name are independent: naming an account never suppresses creating it.

spendCap.description: The spend cap every executor team takes unless it sets its own (ADR-0162): ploegd refuses a claim whose hold would take the team's spend settled in the calendar period (UTC) plus its Runs' holds over usd. Default 20 USD per day. Profile P1 needs every executor team to resolve a cap with usd above 0.

workerSecurityContext.description: The harness container's securityContext. The default meets the restricted Pod Security Standard; {} drops it for a harness image that must run as root.

runtimeClassName.description: RuntimeClass for every worker pod under every executor type; a team's or Role's runtimeClassName overrides it. Empty = the node's default runtime. Under the sandbox executor, executor.sandbox.runtimeClassName is read first.

nodeSelector.description: Node selector for WORKER pods, not ploegd (that is the top-level nodeSelector). Empty by default, so workers schedule on any node. Set your own label to keep agent Jobs and their privileged DinD sidecar off control-plane nodes (ADR-0002: no DinD beside etcd).

hmacCapability.description: ADR-0156: issue (default, deprecated) hands workers the HMAC capability beside the transaction token and accepts it; off issues and accepts the transaction token only and needs transactionToken.signingKeySecret (PLOEG_WORKER_HMAC_CAPABILITY).

harnessOutputInLog.description: true copies the harness's stdout and stderr into the worker pod's log (PLOEG_HARNESS_OUTPUT_IN_LOG): the prompt, tool output, file contents and any secret the agent reads then reach every log store and every reader of the pod's log. Debugging only; false (the default) keeps it inside the worker.

sandbox.description: type=sandbox only: runs each Run in a kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox v1beta1 Sandbox created by a launcher pod.

tokenSecret.description: Personal token (pk_…) for reads and write-backs. Empty = the provider logs and no-ops instead of failing runs.

webhookSecret.description: Verifies X-Signature on POST /webhooks/tracker/clickup. ClickUp generates this on webhook registration — capture it, never invent it. Empty = deliveries are rejected.

doneStatus.description: List status name applied when a Shift finishes, e.g. 'for review'. Statuses are per-List custom strings; empty leaves the board untouched.

apiUrl.description: GitHub REST API root; empty = https://api.github.com. GitHub Enterprise Server uses https://<host>/api/v3.

appId.description: GitHub App id. With appPrivateKeySecret it enables issue reads and write-backs through repository-scoped installation tokens (issues:write, metadata:read).

appPrivateKeySecret.description: The GitHub App's PEM private key. Required with appId.

webhookSecret.description: Verifies X-Hub-Signature-256 on POST /webhooks/tracker/github. Empty = deliveries are rejected.

teamLabelPrefix.description: Label prefix that names a Team on an issue; empty = 'ploeg:'.

teamMap.description: Comma-separated login=team pairs: assigning one of these GitHub users dispatches the issue to that Team.

config.description: ploegd's routing and roster as a file (mounted at /etc/ploeg/ploeg.yaml). Projects are NAMED and resolved to tracker ids at boot, so no magic numbers live in cluster config. `targets:` registers repositories a `repo/<key>` label may select, and a project's `default:`/`allow:` name them (ADR-0038). A project's `gates:` maps its statuses or bucket titles to the delivery gates development, test, acceptance and done (ADR-0051), and Ploeg records every tracker status move of a project with `gates:` (ADR-0080). A target's or project's `ci.waitTimeout:` is how long a Shift on that repository waits for the forge's CI on its pull request's head before a person is asked, default `60m` (ADR-0119). A target's or project's `fastCheck:` lists the repository's fast check, shell command lines a writing Run runs after it rebases onto the base branch and the worker runs before it pushes a rebase of its own; omitted, a rebase is pushed with the check recorded as skipped (ADR-0146). A team's `forgeFollowUps.rebaseOnConflict: true` queues a rebase Follow-Up when a pull request in review is confirmed conflicting with its base (ADR-0146). A team's `forgeFollowUps.reworkOnChangesRequested: true` sends work back on a request for changes only from a reviewer listed in `reworkReviewers` or reported by the forge with write access, at most `maxReworks` times per Work Item, default 3; any other request is refused and audited (ADR-0151). On a Forgejo target, list the reviewers in `reworkReviewers` rather than give the bot admin: Forgejo shows another login's repository permission only to an administrator. A target's `readPullRequests:` lists routes: the `authors` whose open pull requests a `team` reads and reports on, on the pull request, with the operator's `instructions` and `maxOpen` and `maxReviewsPerPullRequest` caps (ADR-0109). A team's `premiseCheck: {model: <gateway model>}` runs one classifier call on that model before its first writer, and ploegd refuses a model the gateway does not price at zero (ADR-0123). The Run card keys `cards`, a target's or project's `cardStyle`, `release`, `rarity` and `cardShape`, a project's `statusKinds` and a team's `cards` and `workingHours` are unknown keys that fail the boot (ADR-0080). A team's `sponsor:` is the person (Ploeg's person id) its Runs act for when nobody handed the work over; with transactionToken.signingKeySecret a Team without one runs nothing (ADR-0156). Empty = the legacy PLOEG_TARGET_MAP/PLOEG_TEAM_MAP/PLOEG_TEAM_PLANS env vars still apply.

usd.description: The most the team's Runs may settle and hold in one period, in USD. 0 = no cap.

period.description: The calendar period in UTC; a week starts on Monday.

networkPolicyPeers.description: A list of NetworkPolicyPeer objects: `podSelector`, `namespaceSelector` or `ipBlock`, as in `networking.k8s.io/v1`.

networkPolicyPorts.description: A list of NetworkPolicyPort objects: `protocol` and `port`, as in `networking.k8s.io/v1`.

networkPolicyIngressRules.description: A list of NetworkPolicyIngressRule objects, appended to the policy as written.

networkPolicyEgressRules.description: A list of NetworkPolicyEgressRule objects, appended to the policy as written.

networkPolicyEndpoint.description: Where one kind of endpoint lives. Empty `peers` derives the destination from each configured URL; set, they replace it for every URL of the kind. Empty `port` is each URL's port, or 443 for https and 80 for http; set, it replaces it, which a Service whose port differs from its pods' needs.

goMemLimit.description: GOMEMLIMIT for a Go container: empty = 90% of its memory limit, a Go size sets it, off renders none

sandboxOverride.description: type=sandbox only: overrides executor.sandbox for one team's or Role's SandboxTemplate, field by field. An unset field falls back to the same tier's runtimeClassName, then the next tier.

runtimeClassName.description: RuntimeClass for the agent-sandbox pod, read before the same tier's runtimeClassName under the sandbox executor only; empty = that runtimeClassName, then the next tier (Role, team, executor.sandbox, executor).

planner.description: ADR-0031: the Role splits or clarifies its Work Item and returns createdWorkItems instead of code. A planner never writes.

shadow.description: ADR-0096: a reading Role whose verdict and findings are recorded and never act. It runs beside a reading Role that is not a shadow, needs its own cap, never writes or plans, and its cost counts against the pool like any Run. Use it to compare a reviewer model on real work.

runtimeClassName.description: This Role's worker RuntimeClass under every executor type. Empty = the team's, then executor.runtimeClassName.

workerResources.description: Overrides executor.workerResources for this role's workload. Readers do not build, so a fan-out round need not book writer-sized pods.

dindResources.description: Overrides executor.dindResources for this role's DinD sidecar (only rendered when the role runs harness.dind).

harnesses.description: ADR-0098: narrows the team's harnesses for this Role, by key (acp/<profile> or the Harness name).

defaultHarness.description: ADR-0098: this Role's default Harness key; it must be one the Role allows.

models.description: ADR-0103: the model aliases an admission may choose for this Role's Runs. It must contain the Role's default, model or the team's model. Unset = that model alone.

planRole.//: name becomes the workload suffix (ploeg-worker-<team>-<role>); writes marks the round's single writer (ADR-0010); cap bounds one Run's spend against the pool (ADR-0012); model/maxReplicaCount/harness override the team's values for this role's workload.

harnessContainer.description: Per team or Role: overrides executor.harnessContainer for this workload. separate on a workload with DinD, a credential proxy off or harness claude-environment fails the render (ADR-0138).

dind.description: false (the chart default) renders no privileged sidecar and keeps both credential proxies on for a qualified harness. true adds the privileged docker:dind sidecar, mounts its client certificates into the harness container and turns both credential proxies off for that workload (PLOEG_CREDENTIAL_ISOLATION_OFF_REASON=dind); the render refuses it without acknowledgePrivilegedDind (ADR-0136).

acknowledgePrivilegedDind.description: Required true for a workload with dind: true, resolved role, then team, then executor.harness. It records that the operator accepts that the harness holds the client certificates of a privileged Docker daemon (root on the node) and, with the proxies off, the real per-Run model key and forge token (ADR-0136).

credentialIsolation.description: Explicit per-workload setting for both credential proxies (ADR-0034). Unset = executor.forgeTokenIsolation and executor.litellm.keyIsolation apply to a qualified harness without DinD, and every other workload runs with both off.

default.description: ADR-0098: this entry is each Role's default Harness unless the Role names defaultHarness. At most one entry; none = the first.

dind.description: false (the chart default) renders no privileged sidecar and keeps both credential proxies on for a qualified harness. true adds the privileged docker:dind sidecar, mounts its client certificates into the harness container and turns both credential proxies off for that workload (PLOEG_CREDENTIAL_ISOLATION_OFF_REASON=dind); the render refuses it without acknowledgePrivilegedDind (ADR-0136).

acknowledgePrivilegedDind.description: Required true for a workload with dind: true, resolved role, then team, then executor.harness. It records that the operator accepts that the harness holds the client certificates of a privileged Docker daemon (root on the node) and, with the proxies off, the real per-Run model key and forge token (ADR-0136).

credentialIsolation.description: Explicit per-workload setting for both credential proxies (ADR-0034). Unset = executor.forgeTokenIsolation and executor.litellm.keyIsolation apply to a qualified harness without DinD, and every other workload runs with both off.

claudeCode.description: claude-code harness only (ADR-0139). Rendered only into a claude-code pod.

plugins.description: Claude Code plugins every Run loads (PLOEG_CLAUDE_PLUGINS). The most specific list wins whole; empty loads none.

runIdentity.description: ADR-0149: every hook of the plugin receives a Run identity for this audience in AGENT_RUN_IDENTITY_TOKEN. Needs the top-level runIdentity.signingKeySecret.

telemetry.description: OpenTelemetry collector the harness exports to (PLOEG_TELEMETRY). Empty exports nothing; a non-empty block needs endpoint.

claudeEnvironment.description: claude-environment harness only (ADR-0084): the Team's self-hosted Claude environment and the Secret holding the Team member login that dispatches to it.

loginSecret.description: Secret with the keys refreshToken and scopes (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_SCOPES).

loginVolume.description: PersistentVolumeClaim holding a signed-in Claude config directory, mounted as PLOEG_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Wins over loginSecret.

carrier.description: client: the person's own Claude Code carries the Runs (ADR-0112); the chart renders no worker for them and needs no login, only environmentId.

readTokenSecretRef.description: Either empty (no reading Role anywhere) or a complete secretRef. A half-set reference would fail at pod start instead of at render.
